newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge talks near strike deadline.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge talks near strike deadline.

text.p: As a strike deadline loomed over Falconbridge Ltd's Sudbury, Ontario operations on Thursday, analysts said only a prolonged shutdown would have a significant impact on nickel prices.
Falconbridge, Canada's second largest nickel producer, and the union representing 1,400 workers have imposed a news blackout on the talks ahead of Friday's 0800 EDT/1200 GMT deadline.
Earlier this week, Canadian Auto Workers union spokesman Rolly Gauthier said progress had been made, but he did not back away from the union's strike threat.
"There is either a deal or we're out," Gauthier said.
The mine workers voted 91.28 percent in favor of giving their negotiating team a strike mandate earlier this month.
Falconbridge's Sudbury operations last year produced 45,700 tonnes of nickel, 50,000 tonnes of copper and 1,600 tonnes of cobalt, including custom feed.

"Falconbridge is not anywhere near the same size a producer as Inco. It would have to be a long strike before it had a significant impact on any of the metal markets," a Toronto-based mining analyst said on Thursday.
Inco Ltd, the Western world's largest nickel producer, experienced a 26-day strike at its Ontario division last month.
The labor dispute shaved US$20 million from Inco's second- quarter earnings and cut its estimated 1997 nickel output to 413 million pounds from a previous estimate of 430 million pounds.
Falconbridge's total nickel production is forecast at 220 million pounds for 1997.
Patricia Mohr, vice-president of economics at Bank of Nova Scotia, said the Inco strike did not prompt a significant upward move in nickel prices.
"When they settled, it was actually a disappointment for the market. There was a price decline there for a while," Mohr said in a telephone interview.
She said Falconbridge likely had sufficient inventories to meet its customer needs during a short labor shutdown.
"Looking at the price of nickel, if they are reducing inventory, it does help tighten up that supply/demand picture if a strike lasted more than a month," Mohr said.
Falconbridge closed down 0.05 at 29.60 on moderate volume of 107,000 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday.
